page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an entry-level instance within the shared ecs.e server family, delivered through the KVM hypervisor on x86_64 architecture. The server provides 8 vCPUs distributed across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with two threads per core. Memory capacity is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per virtual core. Local storage is absent on this configuration, requiring remote block storage attachments for persistent disks, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs or cryptographic coprocessors like SHA-NI are included, though standard AVX and AVX-512 vector extensions are supported.

Benchmark results reflect the shared CPU resource allocation of the ecs.e family. The virtual machine recorded 1,729.79 in single-core stress-ng tests and 7,072.24 in multi-core runs, placing it squarely in the median bracket for compute density. In contrast, instruction-heavy single-threaded workloads exhibit performance limitations, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 859.0 and multi-core score of 4,293.0, alongside lower compression metrics such as single-threaded gzip throughput of 18.66 GB/sec. Cache-level memory throughput tests recorded 570.8 GB/sec for small blocks, scaling down to 80.28 GB/sec read and 49.91 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB uncached buffers.

Cost efficiency is anchored in the shared multi-tenant CPU model. By trading guaranteed single-thread core isolation for resource density, this server minimizes operational overhead for lightweight server duties. It handles general operational tasks effectively, delivering 10.17 GB/sec static web serving throughput and 9.25 million Redis SET operations per second. Tradeoffs include potential performance variance during peak hypervisor contention and low single-core raw execution rates.

Workloads best aligned with the ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge profile include horizontal web serving, non-critical background task queues, development and test staging environments, microservices, and secondary database or cache replicas where strict single-thread throughput guarantees are not mandatory.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is a shared compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM. It features 8 vCPUs derived from 4 physical Intel Xeon cores operating at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM, offering a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio. The instance includes no onboard local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and provides a baseline network capacity of 1 Gbps with no GPU acceleration. Standard benchmarks show average general compute and caching throughput, highlighted by 9.25 million Redis SET operations per second and a PassMark CPU score of 11,140.77, though single-core Geekbench and compression metrics sit in the lower brackets due to shared resource allocation. This instance is suited for budget-conscious general-purpose applications, development staging, microservice clusters, and horizontal web servers.
